pr_title: net: ip: Fix assertion failure when tcp_send_data() with zero length packet
pr_body:
When tcp_send_data() is called to resend data, but there is no data
to resend, zero length packet is allocated and NULL net_buf is passed
to net_buf_frag_insert() in which assertion fails.

Fixes #36578

Signed-off-by: Chih Hung Yu <chyu313@gmail.com>
pr_comments:
@chyu313 Thank you for the detailed analysis.

> The following is debug message printed in console. send_timer work has already been queued when k_work_delayable_remaining_get(&conn->send_data_time)==0, and then the work is processed.

That confirms what I wrote earlier about the work item being already processed, thanks for checking.

> Then I make k_work_cancel_delayable() be called when k_work_delayable_remaining_get()==0, tcp_send_data() will not be called and "no data to send" condition will not occur.

Actually, that made me wonder whether the `k_work_delayable_remaining_get()` check at https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/net/ip/tcp2.c#L1840 is valid at all. Note that `0` can be returned also when the work is already submitted to the work_q (value > 0 would only be returned if the item is scheduled, but not yet submitted). It doesn't seem right that we prevent cancellation in that case.

> Should we solve this synchronization issue and discard this pull request?

I think that we still need the changes from this PR, regardless of the synchronization issues. A final corner case is when the work handler is already being processed by the work_q, in such case cancellation won't "abort" it. I think though, that a special attention should be put to the work rescheduling at https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/net/ip/tcp2.c#L1075 - when we detect that retransmission is no longer needed, it should be skipped I believe.

issue_context.title: net: ip: Assertion fails when tcp_send_data() with zero length packet

review_comments:
> when we detect that retransmission is no longer needed, it should be skipped I believe.

I add this code so that no more retransmission if no data to send.

The following is debug message after this patch is applied. tcp_send_data() is not repeatedly called when no data to send. 
```
tcp_in: conn=0x567e64b8 send_data_total=0 unacked_len=0 send_timer.work.flags=0x104(queued) uptime=4380
tcp_send_data: conn=0x567e64b8 no data to send, thread='tcp_work', uptime=4380
tcp_in: conn=0x567e69dc send_data_total=0 unacked_len=0 send_timer.work.flags=0x104(queued) uptime=4740
tcp_send_data: conn=0x567e69dc no data to send, thread='tcp_work', uptime=4740
```
Hmm, shouldn't we return <0 value in this case, now 0 value means in `tcp_resend_data()` that it will increase the retry counter but in this case there is nothing to send.
I agree, plus I'd add a log message here, so that it's visible how often this occurs.
IMHO `NET_DBG()` is enough here, this is not a very serious issue. Is there an easy way to trigger this condition, how are you testing this?
32 TCP clients running on host send data to 32 TCP echo server threads running on native posix, same test as in #32564.

2 TCP clients sending data to 2 TCP echo server threads can trigger this condition. 
I add k_uptime_get() in log message to see how often this condition occurs for this test.
```
E: conn: 0x567eaef0 no data to send, k_uptime_get()=5400
E: conn: 0x567eaef0 no data to send, k_uptime_get()=7600
E: conn: 0x567eb414 no data to send, k_uptime_get()=8550
E: conn: 0x567eb414 no data to send, k_uptime_get()=20000
E: conn: 0x567eaef0 no data to send, k_uptime_get()=121700
E: conn: 0x567eaef0 no data to send, k_uptime_get()=152050
E: conn: 0x567eb414 no data to send, k_uptime_get()=243450
```

I just wonder if this is the right place to change the data_mode, or if this rather should be done in the TCP state machine.  This would be achieved if we removed the check at https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/net/ip/tcp2.c#L1840, which as I wrote earlier I don't think is correct. @jukkar I think you have the best insight into the TCP2 codebase, do you have an opinion on this?

That is a good question and I do not have clear answer to this. Tweaking/removing the check on line 1840 might be a good start for a fix. Sorry, but is difficult to give direct answer as there might be unseen consequences when changing the TCP code. So I would suggest we experiment with your suggestion before accepting the changes.

With https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/89212a7fbf5fcd8e4d661c016344ae4bf2d46f53 applying the patch in this pull request, my test described in #32564 did not crash system and the test had run for over 240 hours without problems. If the patch in this pull request is not applied, the NULL pointer access may occur with CONFIG_ASSERT=n.
Ok, I think I can accept the fix as it is then. given that you've put it through so severe testing and it actually helps with the problem.
